original_text: Nutrition¨Oxygen requirements: ¤Obligate aerobes –unable to grow in the absence of free oxygen ¤Obligate anaerobes –unable to grow in the presence of free oxygen ¤Facultative anaerobes –able to grow in either the presence or absence of free oxygen
explanation: Prokaryotes have different relationships with oxygen. They can be divided into three categories based on oxygen requirements: 1) Obligate aerobes, which cannot survive or grow without free oxygen; 2) Obligate anaerobes, which cannot grow in the presence of free oxygen and are harmed by it; and 3) Facultative anaerobes, which are metabolic generalists able to grow in either the presence or the absence of free oxygen.

questions.q: Which term describes prokaryotes that are unable to grow in the presence of free oxygen?
questions.exp: Obligate anaerobes are defined as being 'unable to grow in the presence of free oxygen'.

questions.q: What is a characteristic of facultative anaerobes?
opts: They can only grow in environments containing 100% pure oxygen.
They are unable to perform cellular respiration.
They are able to grow in either the presence or absence of free oxygen.
They only obtain energy through photosynthesis.
questions.exp: The notes state that facultative anaerobes are 'able to grow in either the presence or absence of free oxygen'.
